newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria to liquidate 26 banks, says fin minister.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria to liquidate 26 banks, says fin minister.

text.p: Nigeria will liquidate 26 out of 29 local banks originally declared "distressed", Finance Minister Anthony Ani said.

"I have a list of 26 banks certified distressed before the Head of State (General Sani Abacha) waiting for his approval," he told Nigerian reporters on Thursday in Abidjan, Ivory Coast, where he is attending a meeting of the African Development Bank (AfDB).
"As soon as I have his approval the banks will be wound up," he added.

The banks had failed to meet a March 31 deadline by the financial authorities to raise their capital base to at least 500 million naira, a huge increase from the previous minimum capital base of 50 million naira.
Ani said that out of a list of 29 banks initially certified distressed, three were exempted because they were found to have been wrongly debited by the Central Bank of Nigeria.
The 26 now due for liquidation are those considered to be beyond redemption and constitute about one fifth of Nigerian banks.
"What you should know is that the government is not interested in just liquidating any bank; we have to look at the efforts they have made to improve their solvency," Ani said.
Dozens of Nigerian banks started struggling in the mid-1990s following a deregulation of the financial system which led to the establishment of many new banks in the country.
Over the past two years scores of bankers have been jailed or detained for alleged bogus loans and outright stealing from the coffers of their banks.
